cells.tense: Your hands are on something slow, and you are letting it set the pace.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are growing and one move you will make for it this week, then leave it alone for the day.
cells.core:
Sometimes what needs keeping going is smaller than the plan. There is one effort of yours that is slow, and it gets the pace it actually needs instead of the one that would look better from outside. You can feel yourself holding the push back. None of this looks like much. From where you stand it is exact.

The proof is that you are not running on your last nerve. Whatever is being tended is being tended without taking the cost out of you, and that part is deliberate. What it feeds next will be quieter than the ones it has already lit. Some days it asks you to go slower than your own ambition, and that is the fee — paid, and the thing keeps going.

cells.verb: keeping something going without spending yourself to do it
cells.place: the ground where something is still unfolding

cells.tense: Tomorrow's fire is already under your hands, and today has not grown into it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are tending and do nothing to it today, on purpose — if it is still there tomorrow, keep it.
cells.core:
The things under your hands have not been handed to you yet. Somewhere ahead is the version that is finally under way, and you are living there — managing, checking, making sure the outcome holds before it has had a chance to form. What you mean as care arrives as pressure. People can feel the grip.

There is a warmer version of this, and you have run it before: direction comes from what you feel about the thing, and you stay with it because it is yours to stay with — steady, unhurried. Others pick up their pace around you instead of bracing. Right now the bracing runs ahead of the thing itself, and that is what wears you out before it ever gets to grow.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying tomorrow's fire before anyone hands it to you.

cells.tense: You were standing at something that would not hold, and you never left the doorway.
cells.ask: Set one small, ordinary thing in motion this week — a step with a finish you can see — and let what moves be enough.
cells.core:
You know how to keep something going — you have done it, and some of it is still running. Lately you are alert and present and not in contact with it. When a step is suggested, you notice reasons to wait. The work you want is smaller than it is being made to look. Less impressive.

What runs on empty is the part that was supposed to do the pushing, so pushing yourself at it harder is not the way in. What restarts it is a plain ending kept — a small thing set down or handed on. It will feel like almost nothing until someone depends on it.

cells.tense: The work is moving, and you would call it something the situation asked for.
cells.ask: Tell one person, in one sentence, the care that is behind something you have been calling your work.
cells.core:
Somewhere in what you are building there is a hand nobody has named. It shows in what you notice early, what you refuse to let drop, what you keep going when the room has moved on. You call it a task that had to be done. That is the part you are not saying. It is steady work, and it can run without any admission.

What it carries is a direction you did choose, and you are doing the real thing under a cover story. You can keep the cover. That is allowed. But somewhere the honest version of it is easier to stand behind.
cells.sheetLine: You are already keeping something going. You have just not said so.
cells.verb: keeping something going without spending yourself to do it
